Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Finn Allen and Devon Conway to open for the Kiwis. Arshdeep Singh to start with the ball.
...The Chase...

Right then! The pitch is good enough to bat on. Not that bad at all. New Zealand will be aware of the inexperience India possess in the bowling line but should not take it lightly at all. They have to work hard to go in front in the series. Stay tuned for the chase.

New Zealand will feel they have let the game slip away a bit. A couple of partnerships have not helped them. First of all, they didn't start well, leaking many runs and not creating pressure. They bossed the middle phase but not for long as India repaired things up very quickly. Kane Williamson kept on shuffling his packs but only Lockie Ferguson stood out. He took three wickets and so did Tim Southee but he went for plenty of runs.

Excellent recovery from India and a good finish help them get over the 300-mark. At one point, it looked difficult as the Kiwis had all control in the middle overs, India started really well with both openers notching a fifty, they gave a good start to carry on with the momentum but lost wickets in a flurry in the middle phase. A handy partnership between Iyer and Samson helped India get back on track though. Samson fell after playing a decent cameo. Iyer who was struggling earlier took his time before launching. He played a really good inning but it was due to Washington Sundar's surprising quick cameo that helped India get over the 300-mark.

OUT! Wicket of the last ball! Full and outside off. Shardul Thakur looks to go downtown but gets an outside edge to Tom Latham who dives to his right, and takes a brilliant catch. That was rising but Latham did really well. INDIA END WITH 306.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Latham b Tim Southee

Commentary.Commentary: Length and on middle, eased to long on for a single.
FOUR! What a shot! Short in length, outside off. Sundar punches on the up off the back foot through covers for a boundary.
Very full and on middle. Shardul Thakur paddles it to square leg for a single.

OUT! TAKEN! End of a fine innings from Iyer! Short of a length and outside off. Iyer pulls it straight in the hands of Devon Conway at deep mid-wicket. A classy innings from him. Paced his innings really well.
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Conway b Tim Southee

Commentary.Commentary: Full ball, around off. Iyer looks to flick on leg side but gets a leading edge and it falls safely to the mid on region. Two runs. 300 up.
SIX! Sundar, you beauty. 17 runs off the over. What an excellent over for India. Short again, outside off. Sundar pulls it high over mid-wicket for a six.
FOUR! Sundar showing his ability with the bat! A full toss, outside off. Sundar steps across, paddles it over short fine leg for four more.
FOUR! Short in length and outside off. Sundar pulls it in the gap, to deep mid-wicket for a boundary. The player dives but to no avail.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
Full and outside off. Sundar pushes it through covers for a single.
On a length and outside off. Sundar slashes and misses.
Wide! Full ball, way outside off, going down. Sundar lets it go.
FOUR! In the gap! Full ball on middle. Iyer whacks it to deep square leg for a boundary.
Iyer shuffles across and Milne follows him on the leg side. Iyer leaves it and the ball goes through his legs.
Full and on middle, pushed back to Milne, to his left. A slight misfield and a single is taken.
Leg bye! Full and on middle, Iyer looks to flick but misses. It goes to square leg for a leg bye,
On the pads, flicked to deep square leg for one.
SIX! Cheeky! Short in length and outside off. Sundar hangs back, waits for the ball to arrive and dabs it all the way over third man for a six.
FOUR! Ends the over with a boundary! Iyer giving a good finish! This is full and around off. Iyer heaves it over mid-wicket for four runs.
Full and outside off, lack of pace. Sundar chips it in the air and to covers for a single.
SIX! That is a really good strike! This is full and slanting on middle. Sundar waits on the back foot and thumps it back over long on for a biggie.
Length ball, outside off. Sundar drives it to point where the fielder makes a good stop.
On middle, punched to long on for a single.
Outside off, guided to third man for one.
On middle, Washington Sundar pulls it to sqare leg for one.
Full and on off. Blocked out.

OUT! TAKEN! Glenn Phillips with an excellent catch! New Zealand break the 94-run stand! This is full and angling on middle. Samson stays back as he swings his bat but mistimes his shot. He hits in the mid-wicket region. Three players converge with Glenn Phillips running in from the deep, he calls, dives to his left and takes a splendid catch. Just brilliant.
Commentary.Howout: c Glenn Phillips b Adam Milne

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Third of the over. Tries the slower one bowls down the leg side.
Full and on leg. Iyer works it to long on for a single.
Wide! Full ball, straying down. Iyer misses his clip.
Drop and run! Length and on off. Samson taps it on the deck and runs across quickly.
On middle, length and it is played to deep square leg for a single.
Wide! Down the leg side. Wided.
On middle, Iyer tries to heave but gets an inside edge to fine leg for a run.
FOUR! Iyer is clearly the aggressor now. Short in length and on middle. Iyer uncomfortably tries to pull but gets a top edge behind the keeper for four.
On a length and outside off. Samson steers it to third man for one more.
On off, kept out.
A yorker, outside off, jammed out to third man for one.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
Two byes! This is again slow, full and outside off. Iyer tries to reverse sweep but misses. The keeper fails to collect and two runs are taken.
Shorter, slower and outside off. Iyer rocks back to cut but gets an outside edge, The ball falls short of backward point.
Fuller ball, outside off, Samson knocks it through point for one.
FOUR! Short ball, slanting on middle. Samson pulls it hard and to deep mid-wicket, in the gap for four.
Slower ball, drops it short and outside off, hit to covers for one.
SIX! Shreyas Iyer changing gears now! Tossed up on middle. Iyer comes down the track, had to reach for it but does so with long levers and hammers it straight down for a six.
Very full and outside off, skids through. Samson looks to push but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Fuller ball on middle, this is driven to long on for a single.
Tad short and on off, pulled to deep square leg for a single.
Short in length and on leg. Iyer bunts it to mid-wicket for one.
Full and on middle, whipped to deep square leg for a single.
Follows Iyer on the leg side with a length ball, this is hit to mid on for one.
Fifty for Iyer! A fine half-century from him. Had to stay for a long time as he was struggling early on. Now, needs a good finish. Short and outside off, cut to sweeper cover for a single.
Angles a full ball on middle. Iyer flicks it to square leg.
Flatter and outside off, it is punched to long off for a single.
Wide! Floated, outside off, turning away. Left alone.
Tossed up, outside off. Samson again defends it.
On middle, defended out.
Outside off, cut to deep point for one.
Full and outside off, driven to the left of mid off for one.
Outside off, again uses the pace and hits it to backward point for one.
Full ball on middle. Blocked out.
Wide! Down the leg side. Samson misses his clip.
Short in length and on middle, Samson pulls it behind square leg for easy two.
Full and on middle, Iyer eases it to long on for a single.
Length ball, outside off, Samson taps it to third  man for a single.
Short again, slower and outside off. Iyer looks to pull but gets a top edge and it falls in wide open space at deep mid-wicket. Two runs. The stand moves to 50 between these two.
Full and on middle, clipped through mid-wicket for a one.
Short and outside off. Iyer pulls it hard and flat to deep square leg for one.
SIX! BANG! Connects this well nicely! Short ball again, outside off. Iyer sits back and pulls it high over long on for a biggie.
FOUR! Good shot! Short in length and outside off. Iyer pulls it over mid-wicket and bags a boundary.
200 up! Outside off, guided to third man for a single.
Angling on the pads, flicked behind square leg for a single.
Full and on middle, blocked back to Milne.
FOUR! Uses the pace again! Short of a length and angling down. Samson pulls it softly past the keeper and to the fine leg fence.
Length ball on off. Samson looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Length ball on middle. Blocked out.
FOUR! Delicately! A length ball, outside off. Samson opens the face of the bat, uses  the pace and places it to the third man fence.
Length and outside off, cut to third man for a single.

In the air and falls safely! This is full and outside off. Iyer shuffles across and looks to heave but slices and it balloons towards backward point. Finn Allen runs back but the ball was swirling and it was a difficult one to take it, difficult for Allen as well. A single.
On middle, nudged to mid-wicket.
A length ball, just tailing around leg. Iyer steps across and looks to flick but misses and gets rapped on the pads. Tim Southee puts in a huge appeal but misses. That looked just going down.
Full ball, outside off. Iyer pushes it to cover. He wants a single but is sent back.
A length ball, outside off. Samson opens the face of the bat and dabs it to third man for  single.
Length ball, outside off. Iyer mistimes his pull to mid on. 10 runs off it.
On middle, on a length. Iyer taps it to backward point.
SIX! BANG! Short of a length and outside off. Iyer makes room, upper cuts it over third man for a six.
A length ball, around off. Iyer blocks it out.
Outside off, guided to third man for a single.
THREE RUNS! A length ball, outside off. Iyer slaps it to deep cover, to the longer side and the man from deep point runs across and cuts it off. A single saved.
On middle, drilled to long on for one.
Fuller, flighted, outside off. Samson drives it to covers for a single.
Fuller ball, on off. Samson blocks again.
On middle, defended on the front foot.
Full and on off, kept out.
Around off, pushed to covers for a single.
On middle, blocked out.
FOUR! Edged! On a length and around off. Samson looks to defend with an angled bat but gets an inside edge and goes past the leg pole for four runs.
Beaten! Lovely! This is full and slanting around off. Samson tries to play with the angle to leg side but misses.
A length ball, around off. Iyer dabs it to third man for a single.
Back of a length and on middle. Iyer fends it to the right of the bowler.
Short in length and on off. Defended out.
5 singles then! Full and around off, flighted. Iyer skips down and mistimes his heave through mid-wicket for one.
Another single as this is hit through covers.
Tossed up on middle, flicked to deep mid-wicket for one.
Samson is off the mark, full and on off, pushed to long off for one.
Touch short and outside off. Iyer slaps it to deep cover for a single.
Flatter and outside off, punched to cover.
On a length and on middle. Defended out. Two wickets, 8 runs off the over.
Sanju Samson is the new man in.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! The crowd erupts again but this time it is the New Zealand fans who erupt. Beautifully from Lockie Ferguson. He drags his length back and serves it outside off. Suryakumar is on his toes as he looks to punch but finds the outside edge and it flies before sticking in the hands of Finn Allen at first slip. He doesn't make a mistake and India now find themselves in a difficult position.
Commentary.Howout: c Finn Allen b Lockie Ferguson

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off. Suryakumar shoulders arms.

FOUR! This is SKY for you. When others fail to time, he brings all class with him. Pitched up, outside off. Suryakumar leans and drives it through covers to get off the mark with a boundary. The crowd erupts after a very long time.
Suryakumar Yadav comes in.

OUT! BOWLED! Pant was not just able to time well. He was struggling. Short of a length and angling around off. Pant was cramped for the room as he tries to pull. He was a fraction late as well and gets an inside edge back into the stumps. New Zealand keep India on the back foot.
FOUR! A full toss down the leg side and Pant just helps it on its way to fine leg for a boundary. A welcome one. Much needed to be said.
Two more! Quicker, fuller and around off. Iyer clears his front leg and heaves it to deep mid-wicket, in the vacant area for two.
Two runs! Shorter and outside off. Iyer cuts it to deep point where the fielder dives to his left and saves two.
Flatter and outside off. Pant pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up on off. Defended out.
Shorter and outside off. Iyer punches it to long off for a single.
Flatter ball, angling on middle, Iyer nudges it to mid-wicket.
Outside off, this is driven to sweeper cover for one more.
Touch fuller and outside off. Iyer pushes it to cover.
Full and on middle. Iyer drives it to mid on.
On middle, kept out.

Was there an edge? Yes, there was! Short ball around off. Iyer bends his back and tries to ramp over but only gets a faint edge to the keeper. Tom Latham mistimes his leap, tries a one-hander but fails to hold on.
On the pads, this is flicked to fine leg for a single.
Full ball on off. Iyer drops it to covers.
Angles a full ball on middle. Iyer tucks it to mid-wicket.
Good single! Full and on off. Pant drills it to mid off and takes a quick single.
On middle, eased to covers again.
Short in length and around off. Pant pulls it to mid-wicket.
A length ball, outside off. Pant punches it to cover. Not timed well.
Tad short and outside off. Iyer bends and tries to cut but misses. Just one off the over. New Zealand have done well to dominate the middle phase. Mostly after the wickets of both openers.
Too full and on middle. Iyer on drives it to mid on.
This is full and on off, Iyer drives it to cover.
Short ball on middle. Pant pulls and gets a top edge, it flies and falls in front of the running third man for a single. Played with soft hands.
A bouncer now from Milne, on off. It keeps rising. Pant lets it go.
Length ball on middle, Pant pulls it straight to mid-wicket.
Around off, pushed to covers.
Touch short and on leg, pulled away to deep square leg for one.
Length ball on top of middle. Pant defends.
Shorter side at 132 clicks, it bounces and takes the leading edge of Pant who closes the face of the bat too early. The ball falls back on the deck.
Good length delivery on off, skids on. Iyer prods to defend but gets an inside edge to square leg. One.
A length ball, outside off, Iyer knocks it to cover.
Outside off on a length, hit to third man for a single.
On a length and outside off. Iyer splices his drive to deep backward point for a couple.
This is full and on off, pushed to mid off.

A huge appeal for LBW but not given. The only question was whether it is too straight. Kane Williamson takes the review. No bat there. UMPIRE'S CALL it is on wickets hitting. Good call. This was on a length and on middle. Iyer goes back as he tries to defend but gets beaten on the inside edge and gets hit on the pads. That looked close but the bounce helped Iyer there.
A length ball, outside off. Pant cuts it to deep point for a single.
Length and on middle. Blocked out.
Back of a length and on off, defended.
Pant is off the mark! He steps out and mistimes it towards mid on and gets to the other end. He is limping as he gets to the other end. Not sure why.
Swing and a miss! Shorter and on middle, Pant looks to pull but misses. It goes over middle pole.
That is good pace! Length and around off, this lands and moves away. Pant is beaten as he tries to defend.
A confident pull shot! On the body, this is pulled down to fine leg for one.
SIX! Over the fence! This is short and on middle, Iyer upper cuts it and it sails over the third man fence. Really good batting and this should make Iyer feel better.
On the stumps, kept out.
Back of a length and on off, defended.
EDGY FOUR! Not sure why there is no slip for a new batter! Shorter and outside off, Pant looks to push at it, this flies off the outside edge and it goes down to the third man fence.

OUT! TAKEN! Two in two overs for the Kiwis and they are back in the game! This is an area Dhawan where Dhawan scores a lot of runs but also gets out. Southee strikes and the two bowlers who were got back by Williamson for breakthroughs, have provided it. This is full and outside off. Dhawan opens the face of the bat and looks to carve it past point but Allen there takes a sharp catch. Both the set batters back in the hut now.
Commentary.Howout: c Finn Allen b Tim Southee

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish and on off, this is guided to point.
On off, this is pushed to cover.
Back of a length and on off, Iyer guides it to point. It is a wicket maiden.
Another dot! Can this be a wiket maiden? Outside off, Iyer mistimes it towards cover.
That is brave from Iyer! He just came in, looks to make room, Ferguson bowls it on a length and on middle. Iyer slashes but misses. It goes just over the stumps.
Back of a length and on middle, defended.
Goes full and on the pads, Iyer works it to square leg.

OUT! TAKEN! That is a decent catch by Devon Conway and Lockie Ferguson strikes on his return! A welcome wicket for the Kiwis as these two were scoring freely. Gill will be disappointed, it is not the best of balls. It is on the pads. Gill flicks it uppishly towards square leg. Conway runs to his right and takes it nicely. A good innings by Gill but he would have wanted more. Can the Kiwis build on this now?
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Conway b Lockie Ferguson

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Deft! This is outstanding from Dhawan! He is in his elements! Shorter and just around off, Dhawan waits, opens the face and guides it fine on the off side. Another boundary.
FOUR! Hammered away! Short and on middle, Dhawan rocks back and hammers it through mid-wicket. This one races away to the fence.
Fifty for Gill! His impressive form in this format continues! Gets there by pushing this ball towards mid off for one.
Angled into the pads, Dhawan works it towards deep square leg for one.
Fuller and on middle, Gill works it to mid on and takes one.
Good length and on off, Gill pushes it to covers.
Shorter and on off, Dhawan pushes it to covers. Another huge over for India.
FOUR! Runs are flowing now! Dhawan walks across, this is fired full and on middle, Dhawan plays the paddle sweep past the short fine leg fielder and into the fine leg fence.
A little too short and outside off, Gill cuts it through point for one.
SIX! BANG! Gill joins the act! He steps out, gets to the pitch of it and tonks it over the long off fence for a biggie.
Shorter and around off, this is guided to point.
Shorter and on middle, this is hit through square leg for one.
11 from the over! A single to end! Fuller and outside off, Dhawan hits it through coves for one.
FOUR! Milne is leaking runs here! He goes short and on middle, Dhawan plays the upper cut, he plays it over the keeper and down to the fine leg fence.
Outstanding fieldng! Shorter and around off, Dhawan guides it towards point. The fielder dives to his right and stops it.
On the shorter side, outside off, Dhawan chops it to point.
Excellent from Daryl Mitchell! This is shorter and outside off, it is guided past point. Mitchell runs to his left, dives and saves two for his side.

FOUR! Up and over! Dhawan is going after Milne here! This is full and on middle, Dhawan lifts it over the mid on fielder and it races away to the fence. Fifty for Dhawan. Back for India and he makes it count again. A big score is on the offer here for him.
A single to end! On middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket for one.
On off, this is pushed down to long off for one.
Slower through the air and on the pads, Gill looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Flatter and on middle, Gill guides it to point.
On off, this is kept out.
Excellent fielding! Shorter and on middle, this is pulled through mid-wicket. Just the one as the fielder gets across to his right quickly.
A dot to end! Fuller and on middle, this is worked to mid on.
Good running! On off, this is pushed to mid off for one.
FOUR! Up and over! This is not good bowling, this is bowling to Dhawan's strength! This is short and outside off, Dhawan cuts it over point and it goes to the fence. Second boundary in the over.
Back of a length and on off, defended.
On the pads, Dhawan looks to flick but misses. It hits the pad, Latham dives to his right and stops it. A scoring opportunity goes abegging.
FOUR! Runs flowing now! Shorter and outside off, Dhawan cuts, it flies off the top edge and wide of the third man fielder for a boundary.
Shorter and outside off, Gill cuts it past point and takes two.
Excellent fielding! On middle, Gill drags it against the turn wide of long on. THe fielder runs to his right, dives and keeps it down to two.
Quicker and on middle, Dhawan pulls towards deep square leg for one.
Slower through the air, it lands on off and turns back in. Dhawan works it to squar leg.
Tossed up on off, Gill pushes it down to long off for one.
On middle, this is pulled but to mid-wicket.
Dhawan will probably feel he missed out there! A good start by Milne! Dhawan steps out and makes it into a full toss, he hits it hard but to mid off.
Length and on middle, Dhawan gets right behind the line and defends.
Angled into the pads, Gill works it towards fine leg and takes one.
Just short! That held in the surface! On middle, Gill looks to push at it, it goes uppishly but short of the fielder at mid on.
Goes full again and on middle, Gill works it to mid-wicket.
Fuller and on off, Dhawan plays it through covers for one.
Ends the over well! Flatter and on off, Gill guides it to point.
On off, this is pushed to the left of the bowler who dives and stops it. Saves a run.
Sees Dhawan come down the track and shortens the length. This is pulled through mid-wicket for one.
On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.
Dhawan moves across and Santner slows it up, it is a low full toss, Dhawan sweeps it towards short fine leg.
Shorter and outside off, Gill pushes it through covers for one.
FOUR! Clipped away! That is the kind of over India needed and they will hope this gets them going! On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for a boundary.
FOUR! Cracked away! This is short and wide outside off, Dhawan just opens the face of the bat and guides it past point. No chance for the fielder in the deep.
WIDE! Just past the leg pole! Dhawan moves across again, Ferguson goes full and looks to hit the leg pole but misses. Wided.

Really good cricket all-around! Dhawan moves right across, Ferguson goes full and on off, this is worked through square leg. The fielder gets across to his left quickly, slides and stops it. The batters go for two, Dhawan has to hurry and he does make it in the end.
Fuller and on middle, Gill pushes it to mid on and gets to the other end.
Bangs it short and on middle, this is pulled through mid-wicket for two.
Back of a length and on off, Gill guides it to point.
A single to end a tidy first over from Mitchell Santner! On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
Steps out and now pushes it down to long on for one.
On middle, Dhawan tucks it on the leg side, Gill wants one but is sent back.
Works it with the angle through mid-wicket and takes one.
Slightly slower and on the pads, this is worked to mid-wicket.
Shortish, some extra bounce, Gill works it to mid-wicket.
Good from Ferguson! Dhawan makes room again and he is followed! Dhawan looks to guide it down to third man but the ball hits the splice and rolls on the off side.
Slashes and misses! Shorter and outside off, Dhawan makes room and looks to cut but misses.
Back of a length and on off, Gill guides it down to third man for one.
Fuller and on off, Gill strokes it but to covers.
FOUR! Excellent timing and very good placement too! Shorter and around off, Gill just used the pace of the ball and guides it past point. This one races away to the fence. Fifty up for India.
Back of a length and on middle, Gill plays it back to the bowler.
On off, this lands and moves away. Dhawan is beaten as he tries to push at it.
Angled into the pads, Gill works it towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Two! Shorter and outside off, this is guided past point for two.
Back of a length and on off, Gill pushes it to covers.
Lands safe! Dhawan steps out. This is full and around leg. Dhawan looks to go over mid off but does not time it that well. Hits it well enough to clear the fielder. One taken.
Well bowled! Sees Dhawan come down the track and bowls it short, Dhawan defends.
Good pace again from Ferguson! Hurries the batter as he bowls this short and on off, Gill guides it to point. Testing stuff from Lockie Ferguson!
Well timed but does not find the gap! Fuller and on off, Gill pushes it to covers.
Slightly shorter and on the body, Dhawan works it down to fine leg and gets to the other end.
That is quick! Good steam from Lockie Ferguson! Back of a length and around off, this one whizzes through. Dhawan is beaten as he tries to defend.
Slightly shorter and outside off, Dhawan looks to cut but misses.
Outside off, this is guided down to third man for one.
A dot to end then! A sedate start for India in Powerplay 1. They are 40 for 0 after it. On off, angling away. Dhawan lets it be.

Was that a chance? It is! That has been out down! This is fuller and outside off, Gill looks to go over cover but it flies off the outside edge. Goes towards third man. Ferguson runs in, dives forward and looks to take it inches above the ground but does not hang on. Good try but you would expect him to take it. A single in the end. A life for Gill.
On middle, Gill works it to mid-wicket.
SIX! This one sails over the fence! Very smart shot. This is short and on off, Gill waits and then just helps it over the keeper and it flies over the third man fence for a biggie.
Fuller and on middle, Gill works it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length and around off, Gill guides it to point.
Five from the over then! Fuller and on off, this is pushed to mid off.
Yes and no situation but no harm done! On the pads, Dhawan nudges it towards square leg and wants a run but is sent back.

FOUR! EDGY! That has raced away. Really short boundary there, absolutely no chance for the fielder! Length and on off, this moves away. Dhawan looks to defend, this goes off the outside edge down towards third man. The fielder had no chane despite not being very far away from the ball.
Back of a length yet again and on off, Dhawan blocks it.
Bangs it short, gets it to bounce nicely, Dhawan takes one hand off the handle and defends.
Outside off, Gill opens the face of the bat and guides it down to third man for one.
Just the single from the over then! Excellent from Henry again! On off, Dhawan pushes it to cover.
Length yet again and on off, Dhawan plays it late and right under his eyes.
Another one on a length and around off, Gill plays it late and towards third man for one.
Length again and on off, Gill pushes it to covers.
Bangs it short, changes the length, Gill initially looks to pull but then bails out.
Solid! On a length and around off, Gill blocks.
Around off, Dhawan opens the face of the bat and guides it to point. Just the boundary from the over then.
Good length and on off, Dhawan pushes it towards cover.
Fuller again but this time on middle, Dhawan plays it back to the bowler.
The tempter, fuller and well outside off, Dhawan shoulders arms to it.
FOUR! That is a poor delivery! It is short and on middle, sits up to be hit. This time Dhawan rocks back and hammers it through square leg for a boundary.
First real short ball of the game. Dhawan stands tall and defends.

SIX! He can't! Over the fence for the first biggie and India will hope that gets GIll going. On middle, he whips it down the ground and over the long on fence. Short boundaries there and Gill clears it easily.
On the off pole, Gill lets the ball come to him and plays it to point. Can he end the over well now?
Continues to land it on a length and on off, Gill pushes it to mid off.
A little straighter this time, Dhawan works it to mid on and gets to the other end.

Brilliant from Henry again! Dhawan too played that well. This lands on off and then moves away. Dhawan looks to defend but is beaten again. The good thing by Dhawan was, he did not reach out for it. He kept the ball close to his body.
That is a top nut! This lands around off, it pitches and then moves away. Dhawan is beaten as he tries to defend. Henry has been excellent so far.
Two good deliveries to end! This lands outside off and it comes back in a little. Not enough though to make the batter play.
Some nice shape away from the batter, it is outside off though and it is left alone.
Dhawan seems to be going after Southee here! He gives him the charge again. Southee, from around the wicket, bangs it short and outside off, it is cut down to third man for one.
On the fuller side again, Gill pushes it wide of cover for one.
The outfield did not seem very fast there! This is fuller and around off, Gill strokes it through covers. The ball slows up as it nears the ropes, two taken.
On off and on a length, Gill pushes it to covers.
We do have a maiden! Excellent from Henry! Length and outside off to end, Dhawan leaves it alone.
Five dots in a row! Fuller and on off, Dhawan pushes it to cover. Can we have a maiden?
Yet again hits the length and on off, Dhawan guides it to point.
On middle, Dhawan hangs back and plays it back to the bowler. Relentless from Henry so far.
Another back of a length delivery, just outside off, Dhawan leaves it alone.
Back of a length and on middle, Dhawan looks to tip and run but is sent back.
A dot to end but a productive over for the Indians! The last ball is just outside off, Gill watches it go to the keeper.
On the pads, Dhawan nudges it around the corner and takes one.
Gill is now off the mark! This is fuller yet again and around off, Gill pushes it wide of mid off and takes one.
A quick run! Slightly fuller again and on off, Dhawan pushes it to mid off and gets to the other end.
Yet again a delivery which swings back in, it ends up on the pads, Dhawan works it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! That is a beautiful shot! Dhawan takes a few steps down the track and makes it into a half volley, he creams it through covers and the ball races away to the fence. Second boundary for Dhawan.
A really good start then from Henry! Length and around off, this lands and jags back in. Gill looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Just outside off and on a length again, not played at.
Fractionaly full this time and on middle, Gill shows the full face of the bat and plays it back to the bowler. Hitting the middle of the bat there. Should make Gill feel good.
Lands it on a length yet again and on off, Gill plays it to cover. Good from Henry after that wide.
Another back of a length delivery on off, Gill guides it to point again.
Gets it right this time! Length and on off, Gill guides it to point.
WIDE! A false start from Henry! Does get it to shape away but bowls it well wide outside off. Left alone.
Just the boundary then from the first over! This is fullish again and on off, Dhawan strokes it to cover.
Drags his length back now and angles it away from the off pole. Dhawan does not fiddle with it.
Sticks to the fuller line and on middle, Dhawan works it to mid-wicket.
Slightly fuller again, Dhawan pushes it to covers

FOUR! That is a really good stroke to get off the mark! First boundary and runs of the game! This is fuller yet again, it shapes back in from around off. Dhawan shows the full face of the bat and strokes it down the ground and to the long off fence.
Some swing for Southee but it is nicely played! Fuller, it starts around off and tails back in. Dhawan works it to mid on.

Time for the action to begin! The players make their way out to the middle. Shikhar Dhawan and Shubman Gill are the openers for the Indians. Tim Southee to begin with for the hosts with the first new ball. Here we go...

India (Playing XI) - Shubman Gill, Shikhar Dhawan (C), Rishabh Pant (WK), Shreyas Iyer, Suryakumar Yadav, Sanju Samson, Washington Sundar, Shardul Thakur, Umran Malik (On his Debut), Arshdeep Singh (On his Debut), Yuzvendra Chahal.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Devon Conway, Kane Williamson (C), Tom Latham (WK), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner, Adam Milne, Matt Henry, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson.

Shikhar Dhawan, the captain of India says he has been at New Zelaand a few times and enjoyed it here. Adds he would have bowled first as he feels the wicke is sticky. Shares this team has played together and hopes to do their best. Reckons he is grateful for the support they get everywhere. Informs about the team.

Kane Williamson, the skipper of New Zealand says it is a good deck and will bowl first. Adds they have to make subtle adjustments from the past match and look forward to the new challenge. Shares the outfield is very good. Informs his team in the end.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and will BOWL first!
PITCH REPORT - There is a good covering of grass. It might dry up as the game progresses. There will be a swing on offer and the team will love to chase here.
The rain has played a big part earlier on this tour. The conditions are overcasts but we expect the rain to stay away for most time and expect the game to go on smoothly.

India have rested few key players and are giving young players an opportunity with Dhawan to lead them. New Zealand on the other hand are starting the preparation for the next big event here itself as they are coming with a strong squad. On paper, the Kiwis do fancy but these young Indians will be keen to grab a place for the longer road. Stay tuned for more updates.

After an action packed 20-overs cricket for the past few months, the focus now shift to the next World Cup, to the next assignment and that is ODI cricket. Hello everyone to the first game between India and New Zealand.
...Match Day...

After a brilliant T20I series where we witnessed a hat-trick, a hundred, and a tied game on the DLS method, which is a pretty rare occurrence, we shift our focus to the three-match ODI series between New Zealand and India. The first game will be played at Eden Park in Auckland. We will be seeing an young and energetic Indian squad led by Shikhar Dhawan. This will be an important series for both sides as India starts their preparation for the 2023 ICC Men's ODI World Cup. We may see the likes of Sanju Samson and Umran Malik don the blue jersey. Shubman Gill is in splendid form and will support Dhawan at the top of the order. This will also provide opportunities for players like Rishabh Pant, Deepak Hooda, and Washington Sundar to prove their mettle. They also have the No. 1 T20I batter in Suryakumar Yadav who will fancy his chances to add some more runs in his tally. The Men in Blue will look to continue the momentum after winning the T20Is and show their quality in the longer format as well. New Zealand, on the other hand, will be playing for those crucial ICC Super League points. Kane Williamson will be back after missing the final T20I and take over his responsibility of leading the Kiwis. They have more or less the same squad as the T20Is, but we will see more of Michael Bracewell as he has been in fine form in this format with both bat and ball. However, their batters like Finn Allen, Daryl Mitchell, and even Kane Williamson will hope to get runs under their belts, and if they do so, they could have the upper hand with their reliable bowling attack. The last time these two sides met in ODIs, the Kiwis whitewashed India 3-0, and they will be hoping for something similar this time around as well. The T20Is were affected by rain, and weather conditions here are expected to be a bit overcast too, but we hope that it stays clear and we get some good cricketing action. Will the Kiwis start the series with a victory? Or will the Men in Blue get another one over them? We will find out soon.
